revision:
ONE-ROUND REVISION — preserve the current working composition and implement these bounded changes in priority order:
1. Preserve and clarify intent: Resolve the start-state contradiction by presenting the HUD as an upcoming mission forecast or resetting wave/HP to a pre-launch state. Keep every brief-required object, label, control, state, and relationship visible inside 1280×800; do not trade compliance for a cleaner crop.
2. Establish the reading structure: Create a deliberate left-column sequence by grouping the title, mission brief, and Start Mission action more tightly, with the button directly following the briefing. Reposition and rescale existing elements rather than deleting them; allow one primary focal region, one supporting information tier, and quiet utility controls.
3. Finish the shared system: Rebuild the planet with a deliberate surface vocabulary—clean vector landmasses, controlled atmospheric rim, consistent shadow falloff, and sharper orbital geometry—so it matches the UI's precision. Apply the correction through a small consistent set of palette, type, spacing, stroke, border, radius, shadow, and illustration rules, and repair visible clipping, collisions, weak contrast, or unfinished edges.
4. Add one content-specific expressive payoff: Give each upgrade a distinct functional icon and micro-visualization, make the mission threat visible through a content-specific enemy trajectory or shield stress cue, and develop the START control as a memorable launch interaction while retaining the disciplined command aesthetic. Limit this to the hero and semantically different states; reuse the system tokens and remove arbitrary decoration so it does not create a second competing focal point.
Implementation guardrails: edit the existing self-contained HTML/CSS/JS; use no remote assets, libraries, fonts, APIs, canvas packages, or network calls. Keep the fixed viewport at 1280×800 with no scrolling. Preserve all functioning content and verify small text, edge safety, and component alignment after the revision.
conflicts: Completeness versus hierarchy: retain the fidelity action—Resolve the start-state contradiction by presenting the HUD as an upcoming mission forecast or resetting wave/HP to a pre-launch state.—while using the clarity action—Create a deliberate left-column sequence by grouping the title, mission brief, and Start Mission action more tightly, with the button directly following the briefing.—to tier, group, and rescale the required material instead of removing it.

System consistency versus expression: implement the craft action—Rebuild the planet with a deliberate surface vocabulary—clean vector landmasses, controlled atmospheric rim, consistent shadow falloff, and sharper orbital geometry—so it matches the UI's precision.—as the construction grammar, then permit the expressive action—Give each upgrade a distinct functional icon and micro-visualization, make the mission threat visible through a content-specific enemy trajectory or shield stress cue, and develop the START control as a memorable launch interaction while retaining the disciplined command aesthetic.—only as a bounded, content-motivated hero/state exception.

One-round scope versus accumulated requests: prioritize visible requirement ambiguity and the dominant craft defect first; apply secondary typography, spacing, and decorative refinements only when they reuse the same rules and do not trigger a rebuild.
rationale: The plan preserves every requested and already working element, lets hierarchy determine prominence, uses craft rules as the implementation substrate, and admits a single semantically motivated expressive exception so one revision remains coherent and feasible.
